title.en: Hear both sides of a debate
title.es: Escuchar las dos posturas de un debate

es: Reconocer en un debate escolar dónde el hablante concede un punto, dónde lo rebate y dónde concluye.

teaching.en: Admittedly, phones can help in an emergency, but they also distract pupils.
teaching.es: Es cierto que los móviles pueden ayudar en una emergencia, pero también distraen a los alumnos.
teaching.explanationEs: Admittedly abre la concesión: reconoces un punto del otro lado. El but que sigue abre tu refutación.
segments: Admittedly, phones can help in an
emergency, but they also distract pupils.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, phones can help in an emergency, but they also distract pupils.

teaching.en: I concede that the ban is easy to explain, but it is hard to apply.
teaching.es: Reconozco que la prohibición es fácil de explicar, pero es difícil de aplicar.
teaching.explanationEs: I concede that… es otra forma de conceder; el giro con but viene después.
segments: I concede that the ban is easy to
explain, but it is hard to apply.
teaching.audioText: I concede that the ban is easy to explain, but it is hard to apply.

teaching.en: That is a valid point; nevertheless, teachers need one clear rule.
teaching.es: Es un punto válido; sin embargo, los profesores necesitan una regla clara.
teaching.explanationEs: Nevertheless marca el giro tras reconocer el punto: lo que sigue es lo que el hablante defiende.
segments: That is a valid point; nevertheless,
teachers need one clear rule.
teaching.audioText: That is a valid point; nevertheless, teachers need one clear rule.

teaching.en: Some pupils use phones well, yet a ban is still the fairest rule.
teaching.es: Algunos alumnos usan bien el móvil, pero aun así la prohibición es la regla más justa.
teaching.explanationEs: Yet y even so funcionan como but: separan la concesión de la refutación.
segments: Some pupils use phones well, yet a
ban is still the fairest rule.
teaching.audioText: Some pupils use phones well, yet a ban is still the fairest rule.

teaching.en: To conclude, a ban during lessons is fairer than a ban at break.
teaching.es: Para concluir, prohibirlos durante las clases es más justo que prohibirlos en el recreo.
teaching.explanationEs: To conclude anuncia el cierre: resume tu postura en una sola frase.
segments: To conclude, a ban during lessons is
fairer than a ban at break.
teaching.audioText: To conclude, a ban during lessons is fairer than a ban at break.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento y elige la frase que concede un punto.

choices.text: I accept that homework takes time.
Even so, it builds good habits.
To conclude, teachers should set less, not none.

feedback.es: La concesión reconoce un punto contrario («I accept that homework takes time»); lo que sigue con Even so es la refutación.

hint.es: Busca la frase que da la razón al otro lado antes del giro.

origin.text: I accept that homework takes time. Even so, it builds good habits. To conclude, teachers should set less, not none.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es cierto que el examen fue difícil, pero lo aprobé.»

answer.text: Admittedly

feedback.es: Admittedly abre una concesión: reconoce la dificultad y deja el giro para el but.

hint.es: Es el adverbio que abre la concesión; empieza por A.

origin.text: ___, the test was hard, but I passed it.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Reconozco ese punto, pero la regla debe ser clara.»

answer.text: I concede that point but the rule must be clear

feedback.es: I concede that point reconoce el argumento contrario; but introduce lo que defiendes.

hint.es: Primero la concesión, después but y tu postura.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concede el hablante.

choices.text: That most pupils use phones well.
That phones can sometimes cause problems.
That phones are dangerous at school.

feedback.es: «I grant you that they can be a problem» es la concesión; «Even so…» abre la refutación, y lo de «dangerous» lo dicen otros.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del debate con su función.

Even so, it protects the class.
To conclude, the ban is fair.
For instance, one phone rang during the test.

feedback.es: Cada señal cumple un papel: I concede reconoce, Even so rebate, To conclude cierra y For instance ilustra.

pairs: I concede that the ban is strict.
Even so, it protects the class.
To conclude, the ban is fair.
For instance, one phone rang during the test.

prompt.es: Lee el debate y elige la frase que rebate al otro lado.

choices.text: Some say phones help learning.
I concede that they can, in some lessons.
However, most pupils use them for games.

feedback.es: However gira hacia la postura propia: después de conceder, el hablante defiende que se usan para jugar.

prompt.es: ¿Qué concede Leo antes de su refutación?

choices.text: That some pupils may need a phone to walk home.
That a phone in a pocket is still a distraction.
That all pupils walk home alone.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo termina el hablante su intervención.

choices.text: He supports the ban because teachers like it.
He asks for better evidence before deciding.
He asks teachers to change the rule.

feedback.es: La señal To conclude anuncia el cierre: pide pruebas antes de decidir, sin apoyar la prohibición.

origin.audio: I see that the ban is popular with teachers. However, popular is not the same as fair. To conclude, we need better evidence before we decide.

answer.text: nevertheless

feedback.es: Nevertheless aparece tras el punto y coma para girar desde la concesión hacia lo que se defiende.

accepted: Admittedly, uniforms are cheap; nevertheless, they limit personal style.
Admittedly, uniforms are cheap, but they limit personal style.

origin.text: Concede que los uniformes son baratos y rebate que limitan el estilo personal.

To conclude, the school should decide.

feedback.es: Even so gira contra el punto anterior; I concede reconoce y To conclude cierra.

answer.text: valid

feedback.es: Even so va al principio y abre la refutación; después viene la frase completa.

title.en: Much as I admire the plan
title.es: Por mucho que admire el plan

es: Formar concesivas avanzadas con much as, however + adjetivo y adjetivo + as/though en lugar de although.

teaching.en: Much as I admire the plan, I think the fee is too high.
teaching.es: Por mucho que admire el plan, creo que la cuota es demasiado alta.
teaching.explanationEs: Much as + sujeto + verbo equivale a «por mucho que»; el verbo va en presente normal, sin subjuntivo.
segments: Much as I admire the plan, I
think the fee is too high.
teaching.audioText: Much as I admire the plan, I think the fee is too high.

teaching.en: However tempting the offer is, we cannot accept it this year.
teaching.es: Por muy tentadora que sea la oferta, no podemos aceptarla este año.
teaching.explanationEs: However + adjetivo + sujeto + verbo: el adjetivo va pegado a However y el sujeto antes del verbo.
segments: However tempting the offer is, we
cannot accept it this year.
teaching.audioText: However tempting the offer is, we cannot accept it this year.

teaching.en: Strict though the rules seem, they protect every neighbour.
teaching.es: Aunque las normas parezcan estrictas, protegen a todos los vecinos.
teaching.explanationEs: Adjetivo + though/as + sujeto + verbo: el adjetivo pasa al principio.
segments: Strict though the rules seem,
they protect every neighbour.
teaching.audioText: Strict though the rules seem, they protect every neighbour.

teaching.en: Clever as the idea is, it has one serious flaw.
teaching.es: Por ingeniosa que sea la idea, tiene un defecto grave.
teaching.explanationEs: Con as, el adjetivo también va delante, y la segunda parte no lleva but.
segments: Clever as the idea is,
it has one serious flaw.
teaching.audioText: Clever as the idea is, it has one serious flaw.

teaching.en: However much effort we put in, the timetable will not change.
teaching.es: Por mucho esfuerzo que pongamos, el horario no cambiará.
teaching.explanationEs: However much + nombre + sujeto + verbo: «por mucho… que».
segments: However much effort we put in,
the timetable will not change.
teaching.audioText: However much effort we put in, the timetable will not change.

teaching.en: Tempting as the trip was, Mia said no because of the fee.
teaching.es: Aunque el viaje era tentador, Mia dijo que no por la cuota.
teaching.explanationEs: La estructura también funciona en pasado: adjetivo + as + sujeto + was.
segments: Tempting as the trip was, Mia
said no because of the fee.
teaching.audioText: Tempting as the trip was, Mia said no because of the fee.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por mucho que admire el plan, la cuota es demasiado alta.»

answer.text: Much as I admire the plan the fee is too high

hint.es: Empieza por Much as y no añadas but.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por muy estricta que sea la norma, todos la respetan.»

answer.text: strict

feedback.es: Después de However va el adjetivo, seguido del sujeto y el verbo.

hint.es: Después de However va un adjetivo, antes del sujeto.

origin.text: However ___ the rule is, everyone respects it.

title.en: Follow the argument line by line
title.es: Seguir el hilo de un argumento

es: Distinguir tesis, evidencia, objeción y réplica en un debate escuchado y ordenarlas en un esquema.

teaching.en: My claim is that cars should stay out of the town centre on Sundays.
teaching.es: Mi tesis es que los coches deberían quedarse fuera del centro de la ciudad los domingos.
teaching.explanationEs: My claim is that… anuncia lo que el hablante defiende: es la tesis del argumento.
segments: My claim is that cars should stay
out of the town centre on Sundays.
teaching.audioText: My claim is that cars should stay out of the town centre on Sundays.

teaching.en: The evidence is a survey: sixty per cent of shoppers prefer a quiet street.
teaching.es: La evidencia es una encuesta: el sesenta por ciento de los clientes prefiere una calle tranquila.
teaching.explanationEs: La evidencia es un dato que se puede comprobar: una encuesta, una cifra, un hecho.
segments: The evidence is a survey: sixty per
cent of shoppers prefer a quiet street.
teaching.audioText: The evidence is a survey: sixty per cent of shoppers prefer a quiet street.

teaching.en: In my opinion the street is nicer without traffic, but an opinion is not evidence.
teaching.es: En mi opinión, la calle es más agradable sin tráfico, pero una opinión no es una prueba.
teaching.explanationEs: Una opinión dice lo que piensas; la evidencia muestra por qué los demás deberían creerte.
segments: In my opinion the street is nicer without
traffic, but an opinion is not evidence.
teaching.audioText: In my opinion the street is nicer without traffic, but an opinion is not evidence.

teaching.en: One objection is that older people cannot walk far; the rebuttal is that free buses will carry them.
teaching.es: Una objeción es que las personas mayores no pueden caminar lejos; la réplica es que autobuses gratuitos las llevarán.
teaching.explanationEs: La objeción es el argumento contrario y la réplica (rebuttal) responde a esa objeción.
segments: One objection is that older people cannot walk far;
the rebuttal is that free buses will carry them.
teaching.audioText: One objection is that older people cannot walk far; the rebuttal is that free buses will carry them.

teaching.en: The survey figures support the claim, because they come from shoppers, not from me.
teaching.es: Las cifras de la encuesta respaldan la tesis, porque vienen de los clientes y no de mí.
teaching.explanationEs: Support the claim: la evidencia respalda la tesis y la hace creíble.
segments: The survey figures support the claim, because
they come from shoppers, not from me.
teaching.audioText: The survey figures support the claim, because they come from shoppers, not from me.

teaching.en: An outline of the debate has three boxes: the claim, the evidence and the objection.
teaching.es: Un esquema del debate tiene tres casillas: la tesis, la evidencia y la objeción.
teaching.explanationEs: Al escuchar, rellenas mentalmente un esquema con estas piezas en orden.
segments: An outline of the debate has three boxes:
the claim, the evidence and the objection.
teaching.audioText: An outline of the debate has three boxes: the claim, the evidence and the objection.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pieza del argumento es la frase del texto?

choices.text: Evidence
An objection
A claim

feedback.es: «My claim is that…» anuncia lo que el hablante defiende, es decir, la tesis.

hint.es: Pregúntate si es lo que defiende o un dato que lo prueba.

origin.text: My claim is that schools should start later.

prompt.es: Completa: «Según la encuesta, el 70 % de los alumnos duerme poco.»

answer.text: According

feedback.es: According to presenta la fuente de un dato, que es lo que convierte una idea en evidencia.

hint.es: Es la palabra con la que se cita una fuente.

feedback.es: Evidence es incontable: lleva verbo en singular (shows) y no admite -s.

hint.es: Evidence no lleva -s y el verbo va en singular.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la tesis de la hablante.

choices.text: The town should plant more trees.

feedback.es: La tesis es «I am arguing that…»; el dato de los cuatro grados es evidencia y lo del agua, una objeción.

es: Rebatir con tacto y firmeza usando atenuantes, refuerzos y frases hendidas en un texto argumentativo.

teaching.en: What matters is the cost, not the colour of the new benches.
teaching.es: Lo que importa es el coste, no el color de los bancos nuevos.
teaching.explanationEs: What + sujeto + verbo + is + X pone el foco en X; aquí, en el coste.
segments: What matters is the cost, not
the colour of the new benches.
teaching.audioText: What matters is the cost, not the colour of the new benches.

teaching.en: It is the cost that many families overlook.
teaching.es: Es el coste lo que muchas familias pasan por alto.
teaching.explanationEs: It is + X + that + verbo: en inglés se usa that, no what, tras el elemento destacado.
segments: It is the cost
that many families overlook.
teaching.audioText: It is the cost that many families overlook.

teaching.en: The plan is arguably the cheapest option, but it is not the fairest.
teaching.es: El plan es posiblemente la opción más barata, pero no la más justa.
teaching.explanationEs: Arguably atenúa: presentas la afirmación como defendible, no como un hecho.
segments: The plan is arguably the cheapest option,
but it is not the fairest.
teaching.audioText: The plan is arguably the cheapest option, but it is not the fairest.

teaching.en: The fee is undoubtedly a problem for families with three children.
teaching.es: La cuota es sin duda un problema para las familias con tres hijos.
teaching.explanationEs: Undoubtedly refuerza: lo usas cuando tienes pruebas o estás seguro.
segments: The fee is undoubtedly a problem
for families with three children.
teaching.audioText: The fee is undoubtedly a problem for families with three children.

teaching.en: That is a reasonable point; what I oppose is the timing.
teaching.es: Es un punto razonable; a lo que me opongo es al momento elegido.
teaching.explanationEs: Concedes primero (reasonable point) y destacas después lo que realmente rebates.
segments: That is a reasonable point; what
I oppose is the timing.
teaching.audioText: That is a reasonable point; what I oppose is the timing.

teaching.en: What is essential is a fair price for every family.
teaching.es: Lo esencial es un precio justo para cada familia.
teaching.explanationEs: Essential refuerza lo que consideras imprescindible y la frase hendida lo coloca en primer plano.
segments: What is essential is a
fair price for every family.
teaching.audioText: What is essential is a fair price for every family.

answer.text: In my view, pupils should clean their classroom once a week. Admittedly, it takes time away from lessons, and some parents will say that cleaning is the job of the school. That is a reasonable point, but what matters is the habit we build. It is the pupils who use the room every day, and it is undoubtedly fairer that all of us look after it. Arguably, a clean room also helps us study better, because nobody likes to work among rubbish. Another reason is the cost: it is the cost of extra staff that the school would pay otherwise, and that money could buy books instead. Clearly, ten minutes on Friday is not too much to ask. To conclude, what is essential is that we share the work, because the classroom belongs to all of us.

title.es: Debate por el parque del barrio

es: Defender una postura en un debate vecinal integrando tesis, argumentos, concesión, refutación enfática y conclusión.

teaching.en: As a resident, I claim that the park should stay open until ten at night.
teaching.es: Como vecino, sostengo que el parque debería seguir abierto hasta las diez de la noche.
teaching.explanationEs: La tesis va al principio y dice claramente qué defiendes: I claim that…
segments: As a resident, I claim that the park
should stay open until ten at night.
teaching.audioText: As a resident, I claim that the park should stay open until ten at night.

teaching.en: Much as I respect the council, the petition shows that neighbours want longer hours.
teaching.es: Por mucho que respete al ayuntamiento, la petición muestra que los vecinos quieren un horario más largo.
teaching.explanationEs: Much as… concede y la frase siguiente da el argumento con su evidencia.
segments: Much as I respect the council, the
petition shows that neighbours want longer hours.
teaching.audioText: Much as I respect the council, the petition shows that neighbours want longer hours.

teaching.en: Admittedly, there is some rubbish after the weekend; nevertheless, the playground is used every evening.
teaching.es: Es cierto que hay algo de basura tras el fin de semana; sin embargo, la zona de juegos se usa cada tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Admittedly + nevertheless encadenan concesión y refutación en una sola frase.
segments: Admittedly, there is some rubbish after the weekend;
nevertheless, the playground is used every evening.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, there is some rubbish after the weekend; nevertheless, the playground is used every evening.

teaching.en: What matters is that families have a safe place, and it is the council that must provide it.
teaching.es: Lo que importa es que las familias tengan un lugar seguro, y es el ayuntamiento quien debe ofrecerlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Dos frases hendidas seguidas: What matters is… y It is… that…
segments: What matters is that families have a safe place,
and it is the council that must provide it.
teaching.audioText: What matters is that families have a safe place, and it is the council that must provide it.

teaching.en: If the residents vote for the plan, the council can build a new playground.
teaching.es: Si los vecinos votan a favor del plan, el ayuntamiento puede construir una nueva zona de juegos.
teaching.explanationEs: Un argumento con consecuencia: if + presente, y luego can + verbo.
segments: If the residents vote for the plan,
the council can build a new playground.
teaching.audioText: If the residents vote for the plan, the council can build a new playground.

teaching.en: To conclude, a compromise is possible: longer hours with a cleaning team at weekends.
teaching.es: Para concluir, un acuerdo es posible: horario más largo con un equipo de limpieza los fines de semana.
teaching.explanationEs: El cierre propone un término medio y resume la postura en una frase.

hours with a cleaning team at weekends.

answer.text: As a resident, my position is that the park should stay open until ten at night. First, the petition has four hundred signatures, which shows that many neighbours want longer hours. Second, there is no other playground in this area, so families have nowhere else to go after work. Admittedly, there is some noise and rubbish after the weekend, and I understand that the people who live next to the park are tired. Nevertheless, what matters is that children and parents have a safe place in the evening. It is the council that should clean the park and watch the noise, not the families who use it. Arguably, closing at eight would solve one problem and create a bigger one. To conclude, a compromise is possible: the park opens until ten, with a quiet rule after nine.
accepted: As a resident, my position is that the park should stay open until ten at night. First, the petition has four hundred signatures, which shows that many neighbours want longer hours. Second, there is no other playground in this area, so families have nowhere else to go after work. Admittedly, there is some noise and rubbish after the weekend, and I understand that the people who live next to the park are tired. Nevertheless, what matters is that children and parents have a safe place in the evening. It is the council that should clean the park and watch the noise, not the families who use it. Arguably, closing at eight would solve one problem and create a bigger one. To conclude, a compromise is possible: the park opens until ten, with a quiet rule after nine.

In my view, the park should remain open until ten at night. First, the petition has 400 signatures, so the residents clearly want longer hours. Second, there is no other playground nearby, and families need somewhere safe to go after work. Much as I understand the noise problem, what matters is that children and parents have a safe place in the evening. I concede that there is some rubbish at weekends; nevertheless, it is the council that must keep the park clean, not the families. Arguably, closing earlier would only move the problem somewhere else. To conclude, a compromise is possible: the park stays open until ten, with silence after nine.
